evaluation.final_reason: By round 5 the household endorsed a compromise: no very strong-smelling food on weekday evenings, with weekends allowed. Evidence: Agent A proposed the weekday restriction ('no super strong-smelling food on weekday nights?'), Agents B and C accepted it, and Agent D explicitly conceded ('Okay. Weekends are fine.'). Agent A acknowledged the agreement ('Okay, great. Glad we could agree.').

substantive_insights: The main tension is between individual habitual cooking practices and shared-space externalities (odor affecting rooms/laundry/work).
Framing the rule as applying to everyone (A's shift to 'for all of us') helped convert a defensive reaction into a mutual compromise.
A concrete time-based restriction (weekday evenings banned, weekends allowed) resolved the trade-off between residents' cooking preferences and others' needs.
Explicit acceptance by the previously-defensive party (Agent D) was the decisive step to settlement.
